rules.title: Initiative Petition 25-21, An Initiative Petition to Protect Tenants by Limiting Rent Increases
rules.requirement: Would have repealed the state ban on rent control and capped annual rent increases statewide for most residential rental units. The SJC held in Cella v. Attorney General that the petition could not appear on the November 2026 ballot.
rules.key_value: Lesser of annual CPI increase or 5%
rules.status_basis: SJC ruled on June 23, 2026 (Cella v. Attorney General, SJC-13893) that the petition may not appear on the November 2026 ballot.

exempt_if.text: owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units
newly constructed units less than 10 years old

exempt_if.name: educational_religious_nonprofit_facilities
exempt_if.text: dwelling units in facilities operated solely for educational, religious, or nonprofit purposes

coverage.summary: Applies to most residential rental units statewide.
coverage.exemptions_summary: Exempts owner-occupied buildings of four or fewer units, units under 10 years old, certain publicly regulated units, short-term rentals, and units in facilities operated solely for educational, religious or nonprofit purposes.

rules.quoted_span: Under the proposed law, annual rent increases would have been limited to the lesser of the annual increase in the Consumer Price Index or 5%.

rules.title: G.L. c. 40P (statutory ban on rent control)
rules.requirement: Massachusetts has a statutory ban on rent control. The failed initiative petition would have repealed it.
rules.status_basis: The article calls it the Commonwealth's existing statutory ban and says voters passed the original rent control ban in 1994.

precedence.text: the Commonwealth’s existing statutory ban on rent control, G.L. c. 40P

rules.quoted_span: The petition would have repealed the Commonwealth’s existing statutory ban on rent control, G.L. c. 40P, and replaced it with a statewide cap on annual rent increases for most residential rental units.
